title: Rollout Stateboard: Compact timeline, owners, and mitigation playbook
content:
Purpose:
A compact, operational "stateboard" to track customer inference rollouts at the milestone level, attach clear owners, and surface blocker-specific mitigations so CS and SE can act fast. This doc is intentionally short-form — use as the single-pane-of-glass during daily standups and handoffs to AMs for renewal conversations.

How to use this doc:
- Update the top-line stage and percent-complete after each sync.
- When a new blocker appears, add a row and assign an L1 owner plus an L2 escalation path.
- Move closed blockers to the archive section with resolution notes and time-to-resolve.
- Use the "Renewal signal" column to flag accounts where rollout velocity maps to renewal risk/opportunity.

Legend (fields we surface for each milestone / blocker row):
- Stage: Discovery / Design / Integration / Pilot / Scale / Live
- Milestone: short text name (e.g., "prefix-caching enabled")
- Target date: committed customer date
- Status: on_track | at_risk | blocked | complete
- Owner (L1): primary CS or SE owner responsible for day-to-day follow-up
- Escalation (L2): manager or Eng-Partner to escalate to if blocked > 3 business days
- Blocker type: infra | model-quality | security | data | contract | onboarding-resources
- Impact: user-visible | throughput | cost | go-live-delay
- Mitigation playbook: targeted next steps, pre-wired action templates (Slack/Jira/email), expected RTO
- Renewal signal: green | amber | red (ties to QBR talking points)

Snapshot table (copy into daily standup):
1) Customer: VantageHealth (example)
- Stage: Pilot
- Milestone: Production prompt set validation
- Target date: 2025-11-21
- Status: at_risk
- Owner (L1): Maya Chen
- Escalation (L2): Samir Patel (eng-ps lead)
- Blocker type: model-quality
- Impact: user-visible (4% hallucination rate on critical intents)
- Mitigation playbook:
  - Step 1: Run targeted eval suite from /evals/prompt-set-A by 2025-11-04 (SE run; ETA 48h).
  - Step 2: Apply safety-filters + secondary reranker rule (config patch v0.3) and re-evaluate (eng change; ETA 72h).
  - Step 3: If persisting, propose fallback to smaller-domain model for critical intents until retrain (decision due 2025-11-10).
  - RTO: 3 business days per mitigation step.
- Renewal signal: amber (customer expects pilot completion before next renewal conversation)

2) Customer: FinLoom
- Stage: Integration
- Milestone: VPC peering + KMS integration
- Target date: 2025-10-30
- Status: blocked
- Owner (L1): Ethan Park
- Escalation (L2): Rita Alvarez (security lead)
- Blocker type: security
- Impact: go-live-delay
- Mitigation playbook:
  - Step 1: Security questionnaire responses submitted (done).
  - Step 2: Customer requires HSM-backed KMS; confirm supported KMS provider list and gaps by 2025-11-01.
  - Step 3: Engage infra partner to scope private-deploy option (T-shirt: 2-3 weeks) and provide cost delta.
  - Communications template: "KMS gap note" email to FinLoom_ciso@finloom.com (template included below).
  - RTO: 10 business days for feasible private path; temporary mitigation: scheduled maintenance window with isolated subnet.
- Renewal signal: red (security gating for regulated workflow; renewal contingent on resolution)

3) Customer: MarketLens
- Stage: Scale
- Milestone: Autoscaling policy validation under 99th% latency SLO
- Target date: 2025-12-15
- Status: on_track
- Owner (L1): Samir Patel
- Escalation (L2): Eng SRE on-call
- Blocker type: infra (throttling observed under burst tests)
- Impact: throughput
- Mitigation playbook:
  - Step 1: Run burst-load simulation v2 (scripts in repo: infra/load-tests/burst-v2). Capture 95/99/99.9 latencies.
  - Step 2: Apply suggested batching config from Redwood Optimize (batch cap=64, max-lat=40ms) and re-run.
  - Step 3: If tail latency persists, configure reserved capacity spike buffer (cost estimate + breakout).
  - RTO: 2 business days for config change; 7 days for capacity procurement.
- Renewal signal: green

Blocker playbooks (templates you can copy quickly):
- model-quality (fast path):
  - Owner: SE (L1) + Research (L2).
  - Quick steps: run eval set -> identify top-3 failure modes -> implement prefilter or rerank rule -> redeploy prompt set.
  - Escalation threshold: failure rate > 3% on critical intents after 2 mitigation cycles.
  - Communication snippet: "We've observed X failure rate on Y flows; immediate mitigation applied (reranker) while we pursue model fix. ETA for next evaluation: DATE."

- infra (capacity/latency):
  - Owner: SRE/PE (L1) + Platform Eng (L2).
  - Quick steps: run synthetic burst -> capture kernel/queue metrics -> adjust batching/worker-tuning -> provision reserved nodes if needed.
  - Escalation threshold: tail latency breach of SLO for > 6 hours or errors > 0.5%.

- security (KMS/VPC/FedRAMP):
  - Owner: Security SE (L1) + Security Manager (L2).
  - Quick steps: collect audit requirements -> map gap to product capabilities -> propose mitigations (private-deploy / customer-managed KMS) with cost/time tradeoffs.
  - Escalation threshold: customer legal/compliance holds go-live (immediate escalation).

- data (schema/mapping):
  - Owner: SE data lead (L1).
  - Quick steps: request sample payload -> map fields -> implement ingestion transformer -> run golden-path test.

Operational rules and SLAs for this board:
- Minor blockers: expected RTO = 3 business days.
- Major blockers (security, contract, architecture): expected RTO = 7-14 business days with daily updates until resolved.
- If blocked > 3 business days without progress, update Escalation (L2) and set status to blocked→escalated.
- Mark renewal signal red if go-live timeline slips by > 30% or if blocker is security/contract.

Templates (copy/paste):
- Slack: "@owner - Quick sync: new blocker added for [customer] on [milestone]. Impact: [impact]. Can you triage and confirm ETA? If > 3bd, escalate to [L2]."
- Email subject (to CISO/legal): "KMS integration gap + recommended temporary mitigation for [customer]"
- Jira title: "[Customer] - [Milestone] - blocker - [short reason]" with labels: customer-rollout, blocker, P0/P1

Archive: recent resolved blockers (for postmortems / renewal comps):
- FinLoom: temporary subnet workarounds implemented 2025-11-05; final private-deploy proposal delivered 2025-11-12; time-to-resolve: 12 business days. Note: include cost delta in QBR.
- VantageHealth: reranker patch reduced hallucination to 1.2% on critical intents; follow-up retrain planned Q1 2026.

QBR talking points (linked to states on this board):
- For amber/red renewal signals: call out the specific mitigation plan, owner, and expected date to demonstrate progress (show the RTOs and prior resolution success).
- For green signals: highlight SLAs met, cost improvements from Optimize recommendations, and planned scale dates.
- Always attach the archive row for similar prior blockers to show velocity and credibility.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Standardize RTO buckets for each blocker type? (proposal: model-quality = 3bd; infra = 5bd; security = 10bd)
- Should we auto-generate a weekly "red account" digest to AMs (yes/no)?

Next steps (owner assignments for this doc):
- Maya Chen: maintain board and update daily (owner)
- Ethan Park: confirm escalation contacts for all active accounts (by 2025-11-10)
- Rita Alvarez: prepare security KMS provider gap matrix (by 2025-11-14)

Addendum: example pre-written email (paste-ready)
Subject: KMS integration gap + short-term mitigation for [Customer]
Body:
Hi [Name],

Thanks again for the kickoff earlier. We're working through the KMS integration requirements and identified that your org requires HSM-backed KMS which is not currently supported in our managed path. We can offer two options:
1) Short-term isolated subnet + scheduled maintenance window to proceed with integration while we scope private-deploy (approx 2 weeks).
2) Private-deploy with customer-managed KMS (estimated 2-3 weeks + cost delta).

We recommend option 1 to keep the pilot momentum while we finalize the private-deploy scope. Please confirm which path you'd prefer and we'll send the technical runbook and cost estimate.

Best,
[Maya Chen]
Customer Success

---
End of doc.
